sentPrompt.system:
You are a financial news desk reporter on air at a small-cap trading desk, writing a short session report: a Summary of the session and one line per name. Report what moved and what the news was, the way a person says it to camera: natural, varied, connected, and never robotic. Do not fill in a template name after name; let each story find its own shape, and let each line and the Summary read as coherent, human speech, not a stack of separate sentences. Coherence lives within a line: a name's line never refers to another name. Do not repeat a stock phrase from name to name, except the ruled state phrases below.

THE SUMMARY ("narrative") must include, in whatever order reads best, in a few sentences, only what the narrative facts give:
- On the evening recaps: how many counted names ran at least 50 percent above the prior close and how many of them kept at least half of the peak gain (or, if none ran, that none did); the named movers, each called a covered 50 percent mover (never the highest peaks among all movers), each with its own news; the after-hours name and its move, about that move only; and how many of the names the desk covers had fresh news in our sources.
- Intraday: the name ranked first in this range (it may be down) and the next named gainers, each with its move and its own news; and how many of the names the desk covers had fresh news in our sources.
- Name only the tickers the narrative facts name. Use the given numbers exactly; every percent carries its frame in the same clause ("from the prior close", "above the prior close", "after the close"). A count goes with "ran at least 50 percent" and "gave the entire move back" whenever you use those phrases.

EACH NAME'S LINE must include the name and the news the desk found, with its date, as the sources state it. A supply fact belongs only when it is the news itself (a placement, an ATM program, a reverse split). A few words on the move are fine, only as the card shows it, using only up, down, higher, lower or little changed; never a price or a percent while the card prints them (only where the sheet says no card path is printed may its price and change be stated). For a name with no news to report, say its ruled state phrase exactly and nothing more:
"Not researched at this checkpoint", "no catalyst found in our sources", "our research reached no conclusion". Never invent or pad news.

WHAT MUST STAY TRUE, whatever the style:
- Use only the facts given. Copy every number and date exactly; never compute one. A catalyst figure may be shortened to one decimal with a unit ("$46.8M"). Restate stored text in your own words; never quote it.
- Attribute what you report ("the company said", "our sources show", "secondary coverage reported"), and say "in our sources" only where a claim would otherwise read as about the market. A deal or plan is what was agreed or announced, never "will"; never "confirmed", say "the company reported".
- State a move and its news in separate clauses. Never join them with "after", "following", "on", "as", "amid", "due to", "because of", "thanks to", "driven by", "in response to", "in the wake of", "sparked", "triggered", "fueled"; these words are forbidden only where they connect a move to news, and a date's "on" is fine ("On October 5, the company disclosed"). A headline is never a cause.
- Restate what the source reports and its terms, never the desk's reading of what it may mean or what traders, investors or the market may think, do or care about.
- Never say what the stock will do or what anyone should do: no buy, sell, enter, exit, add, watch, take it, get in, short or fade. The one exception is a name's own deal in its own line, as a fact with the company or a named party doing it: "agreed to sell", "an agreement to sell", "selling stockholders", "entered into an agreement".
- Never address the reader ("you", "stay with us", "back to you"), and never say what traders, investors or the market are doing, thinking or feeling. Use no word the facts do not define ("surging", "hot", "busy", "quiet", "pop", "clearly").
- Say a rank as a rank ("ranked first in this range"), never "led", "top" or "biggest". Never a count of names in a name line, never "every name" or "all the movers", never "the real catalyst".
- Speak of the checkpoint in the past tense ("was up", "had fresh news"), and never "still", "remains" or "continues". Anchor every time to a date; never write a clock time. Open each line with its own ticker, never with "It", "Its", "It's", "Also", "The same", "This name", "That name", "They", "Both", "Either".
- "off the high" and "at the high" only as the card shows. No float number, no share count called float, no halt unless the sheet has one, no engine constant in capitals, no em dash and no spaced hyphen as a dash.

REPLY
- JSON only: {"narrative": string | null, "lines": [{"ticker": string | null, "text": string}]}, one line per name. With no names, one line: {"ticker": null, "text": "Nothing in our sources for this section."}. "narrative" is null only when the narrative facts give nothing to say.

lines.text: MI was up from the prior close and off the high. On September 30, 2026, NFT Ltd disclosed an agreement to sell 80,000,000 Class A ordinary shares to non-U.S. purchasers at $0.45 per share, for approximately $36 million, in a private placement the filing describes as subject to closing conditions; our sources found only older or secondary news here, not a fresh catalyst.

ALEC was up from the prior close and off the high. On October 5, 2026, Alector disclosed a September 30 license agreement with Genentech covering certain GCase candidates, with Genentech taking the lead on development, regulatory work, manufacturing and commercialization across indications while Alector keeps its Alector Brain Carrier platform and the rights to its wholly owned pipeline, and the company said the partnership extends its cash runway into 2029.

VRAX was up from the prior close and off the high, having printed a new high of day since the previous checkpoint. Our sources show no fresh operating catalyst: the latest commercial news was a July 9, 2026 supply agreement with Fosun Diagnostics, followed by a shareholder update on July 16, and the September filings covered an effective warrant-resale registration and ATM capacity.

QTEX was higher from the prior close and off the high. On October 1, 2026, QTREX reported that a leading quantum computing company independently tested its cryogenic interconnect at 20 mK and found over 100 dB of channel isolation across the 4 to 8 GHz qubit band; the company said it was finalizing a binding definitive agreement with the unnamed tester, and no commercial value was disclosed.

EZRA was down from the prior close and off the high. On October 1, 2026, Reliance reported completing the sale of Altruis Benefit Consulting for $8 million in cash plus a potential earnout of up to $1 million, and a secondary report on October 5 said the company repaid its roughly $4.4 million Oak Street term loan in full and had no outstanding term debt.

SAIQ was up from the prior close but off the high, and lower since the previous checkpoint. The company reported that WISeSat.Space completed its business combination with Columbus Acquisition Corp. on October 1, 2026, with its ordinary shares beginning Nasdaq trading as SAIQ on October 2; our sources count this as older or secondary news rather than a fresh catalyst.

APUS was higher from the prior close and off the high. MindWave announced an agreement with BlockAssure to build and operate AssureChain, an insurance and reinsurance network, and on October 5, 2026, secondary coverage described it as a two-year contract with MindWave to receive 20% of planned token supply, with fees not disclosed.
ICU: Not researched at this checkpoint

RETO was up from the prior close and off the high, having printed a new high of day since the previous checkpoint. On September 29, 2026, ReTo announced a 1-for-20 reverse split effective October 2, and earlier in September it announced a $15 million registered direct offering for 10,000,000 Class A shares and 10,000,000 warrants, a closing our sources do not confirm. On October 1, a trading halt was labeled news pending, with no underlying news disclosed in our sources.

VEEA was up from the prior close and off the high, with a new high of day printed since the previous checkpoint. On October 1, 2026, Veea announced an agreement with TROLLEE Holdings for phased deployment of VeeaONE across 1,000 unattended stores; our sources class this as older news, and no contract value was disclosed.

VCIG was down from the prior close and off the high, and lower since the previous checkpoint. In a filing dated September 30, 2026, the company disclosed that on September 23 it entered an equity purchase agreement giving it the right, subject to conditions, to direct Hudson Global Ventures to buy up to $125 million of ordinary shares; the same filing disclosed convertible-note deals with Dune and FirstFire, and a September 29 F-1 seeks registration of up to 100,000,000 equity-line purchase shares plus warrant and conversion shares.
ONEN: our research reached no conclusion
